blocks.text: The Army truck reached the square after the fire crews had put out the last of the burning boards.
Seth was still holding Jaws by the towing chain. The head had tried every direction. Fist had counted the first six attempts, then stopped helping.
Billy showed the soldiers the captured ray. One of them recognized the box at once.
“We need something else first,” Seth said.

The recovery crew bolted a steel equipment cage to the truck bed. While Seth held the chain snug, a mechanic secured a brace around Jaws’s closed iron jaw with bolts, clear of his skin. Seth unhooked the tether from the wreck and put him inside. The cage door locked.
Jaws rose against the bars. The cage stayed on the truck. With his jaw held shut, he could not get his teeth around anything.
Seth checked the last fastening. Two soldiers stayed with the cage for the journey to a guarded vehicle bay.

Laura left separately in a cleared police van, with Jenny watching her face and a fire engine following. At the station, officers had emptied a masonry wash bay. A hose crew waited beside its floor drain.
Jenny warned the guards that Laura could fire without using her hands. She stayed until they had taken their positions with the hose crew.
Laura sat on the bench the officers brought in. When Jenny left, she was watching the water run toward the drain.
Dork went to a different cell. He asked twice who would pay for his tank.
Billy spread his notebook on the hood of a police car.
He had the bank reports, the old laboratory photograph and the route Dork's tank had taken into the square. A delivery driver had seen it come out of an industrial side street.
Billy circled that street on his map. It was already on his list.
The officers checked the address before dark.

Between two warehouses stood the laboratory from the newspaper photograph. The delivery doors were open. Inside, the vault waited on its transport frame, its door swung wide and its locking lug burned through.
Billy stood back while the bank manager and police went in.
blocks.alt: Billy’s notebook and map help police identify the relocated laboratory, where the bank manager finds the open freestanding vault and its remaining bundles of money.

blocks.text: Most of the bundles still stood on the shelves. The manager checked their bands against his records while an officer wrote down each stack.
Billy looked from the open vault to the workbench.
“Check the drawers.”
They found the extra bundles in the drawer beside the cold cutting torch and added them to the count.
The police sealed the building. The vault would go home on a proper truck.
Billy closed his notebook. Four newspaper stories had finally led to one address.
The two tiny police cars waited on a tray at the Army truck.
A technician checked the ray's disconnected lead and tested the selector against the Army instruction sheet. Dork remained at the station. Nobody needed him at the switch.
Seth carried the first little cruiser to the center of a closed stretch of street. Its doors were open. The officers had checked both cars before allowing anyone to move them.
Everyone went behind the marked line.
The technician selected red.
Light touched the little car. Its tires spread across the pavement and its roof rose until the cruiser stood full-sized in the cleared space.
blocks.alt: From behind a clear boundary, an Army technician restores an empty miniature police cruiser with the captured ray’s red beam while the Defenders and officers watch safely to one side.

blocks.text: An officer walked around it, looking through the windows. He pressed one hand against the roof.
“I'll take that.”
The second car came back the same way.
The technician switched off the ray. Two soldiers packed it into its case and carried it into the guarded truck.
Across the square, the tower's windows caught the last light. People had begun walking beneath them again.
Jenny stood beside Seth.
“He'd have liked that.”
Seth looked at the restored cars.
“Yes.”
Neither of them looked away from the tower for a while.
Back at Claude's building, Billy unpinned the cutting about the vault.
He laid it inside his notebook with the others. The red thread came down a strand at a time.
Fist hovered beside the desk. A smear of stone dust remained along his knuckles. Billy wiped it away with a clean cloth.
“Any damage?”
Fist turned so he could see both sides.
“Not to me.”
Billy folded the cloth.
Jenny opened the window.
The room smelled of warm brick and the coffee Billy had forgotten that morning. Below, a truck stopped at the loading door. Someone called for a hand with a crate.
Seth stood beside her. He could still feel the weight of the turret in his shoulders. Once, he would have hurried to tell Flaming Head exactly how much he had lifted.
The space above the sill was empty.
Jenny found the pencil where she had left it before their friend went away. She rolled it between her fingers, then laid it flat again.
“He told us to keep helping people.”
Billy came to stand below the window. Fist settled beside him.
Seth rested his hand on the brick ledge.
“We will.”
The four friends stayed there while the city lights came on.
blocks.alt: Seth, Jenny, Billy and Fist gather quietly at the facility’s open window above Cleveland at dusk, leaving the empty space where Flaming Head used to hover.

blocks.text: Terminal Tower shone beyond the roofs. At the loading door below, the crate scraped over the edge of the truck. Seth turned toward the stairs.
Jenny followed him. Billy set his notebook beside the radio, and Fist went ahead to see who needed a hand.
They left the window open.
